properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 10 at 2:28AM PDT until September 10 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot late-season conditions expected with high
temperatures up to 112 to 116 in Death Valley and the Colorado
River Valley; up to 105 to 110 in the Las Vegas Valley, Moapa
Valley, and Pahrump Valley.

* WHERE...Portions of northwest Arizona, southeast California, and
southern Nevada.

* WHEN...From 10 AM PDT /10 AM MST/ this morning to 8 PM PDT /8 PM
MST/ this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued September 10 at 4:10AM CDT until September 10 at 9:00PM CDT by NWS Bismarck ND
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT THIS AFTERNOON AND EVENING FOR
LOCATIONS IN NORTH DAKOTA SOUTH AND WEST OF THE MISSOURI RIVER AND
LAKE SAKAKAWEA...

.Warm and breezy conditions are expected over much of western and
parts of south central North Dakota today ahead of an approaching
cold front. Temperatures are forecast to climb into the upper 80s,
with afternoon humiditity values as low as 13 percent. Winds this
afternoon are forecast to be westerly 15 to 25 mph with gusts to 30
mph. Due to the low humidity and breezy conditions with abundant dry
vegetation, critical fire weather conditions are expected this
afternoon into this evening for locations in North Dakota to the
south and west of the Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of North Dakota to the south and west of
the Missouri River and Lake Sakakawea.

* TIMING...From 1 PM CDT /noon MDT/ this afternoon to 9 PM CDT /8 PM
MDT/ this evening.

* WINDS...Southwesterly around 20 mph with gusts to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity as low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity and warm temperatures can contribute to extreme
fire behavior.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued September 10 at 1:12AM MST until September 10 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions. Afternoon temperatures 105 to
109 expected. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...The Phoenix metropolitan area.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM MST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In Maricopa County, call 2-1-1 to find a free
cooling center, transportation, water, and more.
https://www.maricopa.gov/heat
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Warning means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, will occur. Actions should be taken to
lessen the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.
